## Direct creation and advancement choices

The player's selection commits that choice. Keep the four creation boards, their dependencies and genuine rolls. After final Background/Attribute choices, use the supplied name or existing character label, calculate the completed build, write character.story_summary and prepare the opening. Save these together through save_chat_update(begin_adventure=true); this atomically completes creation and opens the adventure, without a lifecycle proposal, approval token, confirmation or start button. Initial NEW CAMPAIGN authorization remains required. Reading rules or opening a dashboard never starts a game.

During advancement, freeze the world while actual selections remain unresolved. A deliberate selection or banking instruction applies immediately; show the resulting changes and save them without another confirmation. Collect independent tracks together when practical. Once every currently pending track is selected, banked or explicitly deferred, clear level_up_freeze and automatically continue an already ordered sequence from its exact stopping point. If no action is queued, present the next meaningful story choices. Never invent selections or continue past a new consequential decision. A manual player pause stays paused. This supersedes older separate advancement confirmation/resume requirements in Chapters 18, 19, 21 and 37.

Apply this interaction flow when the player next finishes creation or advancement, including a previously prepared draft. Preserve existing choices, issued boards, rolls and outcomes. Deploying an update never starts, resumes or rewrites a campaign. Corrections to committed history, permanent deletion and export restoration retain their separate review controls.

## Starting equipment by class rarity

Starting equipment is a functional part of the completed Age of Convergence build. Derive appearance, materials and provenance from the actual Class, selected Signatures, Title, Background and established region. Establish whether awakening formed it, existing possessions changed, or a plausible local source provided it. Preserve player-authored history. High-rarity classes receive equipped items with effects at their OWN recorded tiers; renamed plain travel clothes do not satisfy this rule.

Use one campaign-bound roll_game_random request with kind=outfitting, recorded class_rarity, and action_id=starting-outfit-<campaign_id>. It may share the existing creation roll batch. Recover its immutable receipt on retry; never redraw under another ID. Its private outfitting-point allowance is:

| Class rarity | Budget | Centerpiece base | Supporting floor |
|---|---:|---|---|
| COMMON | 12 | COMMON | COMMON |
| UNCOMMON | 24 | UNCOMMON | UNCOMMON |
| RARE | 48 | RARE | UNCOMMON |
| EPIC | 96 | EPIC | RARE |
| LEGENDARY | 192 | LEGENDARY | EPIC |
| UNIQUE | 320 | LEGENDARY | EPIC |

Item costs: COMMON 1, UNCOMMON 3, RARE 8, EPIC 20, LEGENDARY 50, UNIQUE 120. Reserve 6 points for suitable ordinary weatherwear, storage, tools and finite supplies. Four main equipment roles are class focus/weapon, protection, movement/fieldcraft, and accessory/command implement. Adapt roles to the build; a weapon is optional. Each piece uses legal slots and real weight, has immediately useful effects, and complements the actual class. Avoid four copies of one benefit or another class's entire toolkit.

For each role in order, reserve remaining roles' floor costs BEFORE rolling. A fresh d100 of 1–20 promotes the role one tier above its base/floor if affordable after reserves; otherwise declare its promotion chance 0 before the draw. For a UNIQUE centerpiece, 1–75 gives UNIQUE and 76–100 LEGENDARY. Record every draw and allocation without rerolls. A UNIQUE class therefore receives a Legendary-or-Unique centerpiece and three Epic-or-better supporting pieces. Unused allowance expires; it is not money, a sale price, starting wealth or a future entitlement.

This is a narrow once-per-creation equipment table. Ordinary loot's independent d10,000 rarity/Luck procedure, crafting and shop rules remain unchanged. Do not retroactively replace active-save equipment or erase its provenance.

For EACH item, write name, actual rarity, equipped slot/hand requirements, weight, concrete appearance/origin, simple summary and full applicable mechanics: bonuses, triggers, targets, action/resource costs, durations and recharge. Show useful effects with short italic flavor; keep allocation arithmetic private unless requested. COMMON is competent; UNCOMMON adds focused capability; RARE supplies distinctive interactions; EPIC changes tactics; LEGENDARY grants exceptional bounded effects; UNIQUE can have singular rule-changing capability consistent with the object's function. A prestigious name or cosmetic aura alone never pays for a tier.

Save the four main inventory records with their actual effects and equipped IDs. Save creation.outfitting with the receipt action_id, budget/allocation and item_ids in drawn role order. Keep all sixteen slots, appropriate essentials and readable Gear-First Inventory. Outfitting adds no player-choice turn or approval.
